question: In humans, after fertilisation, the embryo is implanted in which part of the body?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Uterus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In humans, the process of reproduction begins with **fertilisation**, which typically occurs in the **Fallopian tube** (specifically the **ampulla** region).
 
• Once the **sperm** and **egg** fuse to form a **zygote**, this single cell begins to divide rapidly through a process called **cleavage** while moving toward the **uterus**.
 
• By the time the developing embryo reaches the **uterus**, about **3 to 5 days** after **fertilisation**, it has transformed into a hollow ball of cells known as a **blastocyst**.
 
• **Implantation** is the specific stage where this **blastocyst** attaches and embeds itself into the **endometrium** (the inner lining of the **uterus**). ***Hence, the correct answer is Uterus.***
